data.title: Nene Royal’s ‘Hysteria’ tops 1 million views
data.description: Thai rocker Nene Royal’s latest performance on ”America’s Got Talent” — a rendition of Muse’s “Hysteria” — has surpassed one million views online within just 14 hours of its release.

data.title: Hungarian masterpieces fit for a Queen
data.description: Under the Royal Patronage of HRH Princess Sirivannavari Nariratana Rajakanya, the Royal Bangkok Symphony Orchestra celebrated the birthday of HM Queen Suthida Bajrasudhabimalalakshana recently at the Thailand Cultural Centre, once again generously supported by B.Grimm and directed most expertly by resident conductor Dr Vanich Potavanich.

data.title: Oldest wild Sunda clouded leopard caught on camera
data.description: Newly-released camera trapfootage from a recentstudy captures the oldest wild Sunda clouded leopard ever recorded, an 8.5-year-old female in Malaysian Borneo's rainforests, offering a glimpse into the life of one of the world's most elusive wild cats.

data.title: More than The Mouse Boys
data.description: Malawi is not well known internationally for its traditional and popular music, although that may change with the release of a fascinating contemporary compilation Sounds Of Malawi Vol.1 (Hen House Studios).

data.title: Webs of interdependence
data.description: For some, a family guides how a person should feel and live in wider communities. In The Analects, Confucius' appreciation of ancestry is conveyed through the image of how a man continues to follow his father's way even after his death.

data.title: Copenhagen Fashion Week garments made from bananas?
data.description: Copenhagen Fashion Week drew to a close with a grand display of brands showcasing their Spring/Summer 2027 collections in the Danish capital. Among the presentations that caught the eye was IAMISIGO, where the pursuit of identity was woven directly into garments through an unexpected vocabulary of materials,,,, including fruit.

data.title: Murder most vague
data.description: Even though the Idaho murder case in 2022 is still remarkably fresh in memory, especially if you have been following the news and social media coverage, the amount of content made about this tragedy is no longer new.

data.title: 'The Thai Interpreter' movie and the reality of Thai immigrants in US
data.description: Although LAAM: The Thai Interpreter (2026) takes us through the eyes of a Thai state interpreter struggling to find her footing in a career marked by injustice and suffering in the United States, it is also a rare portrayal of the bitter reality facing Thai immigrants who dream of a better life in the Land of Opportunity.

data.title: Istanbul cymbals: From Ottoman war tool to pulse of global music
data.description: ISTANBUL - The rhythmic clanging of hammers on bronze echoes through the Istanbul workshop where three craftsmen are landing blows with astonishing precision to transform featureless metal discs into highly prized handcrafted cymbals.

data.title: Thai printmaking in focus at Chok Maa
data.description: Chok Maa, a new artist residency and exhibition space in Bangkok, presents "Difference And Repetition: Contemporary Thai Printmaking", an exhibition celebrating the breadth, craftsmanship and innovation of contemporary printmaking in Thailand, from Saturday to Sept 26.

data.title: Maroon 5 magic returns to Bangkok
data.description: American pop-rock sextet Maroon 5 will head back to Impact Arena for their eighth concert on Feb 9.

data.title: The price of survival
data.description: The new Apple TV limited drama series Lucky is a high-stakes thriller about survival, identity and the difficult process of escaping the life you were born into. At the centre of the story is Luciana "Lucky" Armstrong (Anya Taylor-Joy), a brilliant but troubled con artist raised by her father, John Armstrong (Timothy Olyphant), a charming career criminal who taught her everything he knew about deception and survival -- except how to escape the world he created for her.

data.title: Ukraine marks 35 years  of independence with  Bangkok film festival
data.description: The Embassy of Ukraine will hold the Second Ukrainian Film Festival in Thailand at the Bangkok Art and Culture Centre from Aug 4-6, marking the 35th anniversary of Ukraine's independence. All films in the programme will be shown in Thailand for the first time.

data.description: "Urban Collectibles" returns for its landmark fifth edition to create a point of stillness at The StandardX, Bangkok Phra Arthit daily from 1pm to 9pm, from Friday to Sunday.

data.description: 6060 Arts Space presents "Supernova", an exhibition that takes viewers into a psychological universe where they can move gradually through forces of attraction, memory, desire, conflict, fragmentation and renewal, from Thursday to Aug 29.

data.title: Beyond the unrest
data.description: Chaiyos Pinpradab, founder of the magazine Phuket Bulletin, is now retired and living in his home on the island. Whenever he hears news regarding loss of innocent lives during local unrest, he is heartbroken.

data.title: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' redefines responsibility
data.description: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ (2026) marks a bright morning for Tom Holland’s friendly neighbourhood superheroes. From the promotional trailers, the film is distinctly different in its visual representation than the “Home” trilogy. Yet, what makes 'Brand New Day' great is not in its departure from the others, but how it built on the legacy of the previous ones, including those of Maguire and Garfield.

data.title: LEGO Art recreates Klimt's “The Kiss” in bricks
data.description: LEGO is expanding its Art collection with a brick-built tribute to Gustav Klimt's iconic “The Kiss".
